newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Thorn profits rise, closes some stores.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Thorn profits rise, closes some stores.

text.p: British electrical retailer Thorn Plc reported a modest rise in nine-month profits on Monday but predicted a stagnant performance for the whole year.

The group, which split from music giant EMI last August, also announced the closure of about 90 Radio Rental stores in Britain with the loss of about 360 jobs as part of a restructuring of its appliance rental business.
Thorn recorded an eight percent rise in its nine-month pretax profit to 123 million pounds ($200 million) on a five percent higher turnover of 1.19 billion pounds.
The group said it expected its 1997/97 pretax pre-exceptional profit would be close to its previous year's pro-forma pretax profit of 170.7 million pounds.
The store closures are part of a cost-reduction programme intended to yield six million pounds ($9.8 million), the company said.
"The stores (to be closed) were operating at half efficiency," Thorn's director of corporate affairs Jim Donovan said.
The shutdown was welcomed by investors who pushed the company's share price rose to a session high of 207 pence, up 19 pence. It later fell back to 204.
Thorn's share price had fallen nearly 50 percent since its listing as a separate firm following the spinoff from EMI.

Nick Budd, analyst with Mees Pierson, said the decision to close down the slow-growth Radio Rental units would only underpin a flat outlook for the highly competitive electrical rental sector in Britain.
Return on sales improved marginally to 11.2 percent. The group's net borrowings were also lower at 233.7 million pounds compared with 260 million in the previous year.

Donovan said the group continued to be hit by a sluggish U.S. market which has so far dipped three percent on a like-for-like basis this year. The U.S. accounts for 40 percent of Thorn's overseas operations which had been affected by the strength of sterling.
"It will affect us in the fourth quarter... by about 10 percent," said Donovan on the impact of a rising pound.
The group is setting up more outlets in the U.S. to achieve higher volumes, however. Its main target is the rural sector where, the company said, it had seen "encouraging performance."
The company purchased this month 36 outlets, mainly in rural Illinois, for $12.3 million taking its total number of U.S. stores to 1,396.
Despite its cost reductions, Thorn is sticking to its expansion plan for its Crazy George furniture stores in Britain to 60 shops from the current 54. ($ = 0.614 British Pounds)
